help.cleanup.title: Where to start?
help.cleanup.msg: Choose a preset or individual items, then select quarantine or permanent deletion. Analyze first and review the confirmation. Quarantined files can be restored from Privacy; permanently deleted files cannot. Green means lower risk, yellow means caution, red is for experienced users.
help.optimize.title: What are tweaks?
help.optimize.msg: Tweaks are Windows settings for speed and privacy. A switch turns a tweak on or off. Start with the "All safe" preset. Before risky changes the program creates a restore point, and the "Roll back all" button restores the original values. The REBOOT label means a restart is required.
help.system.title: What are services?
help.system.msg: Services are background programs of Windows. Stopping a needed service can break the system, so core services are protected and the program asks for confirmation before stopping the others. If you are not sure, do not change anything.
help.privacy.title: Whitelist and quarantine
help.privacy.msg: The whitelist holds rules for files the program will never delete (for example, *.log). Quarantine keeps files deleted during cleanup: click the restore button next to a session to put the files back.
help.disk.title: Where did the space go?
help.disk.msg: Click "Analyze" to see which folders and files take the most space. "Shadow copies" are Windows backup snapshots that can take a lot of space; old ones can be deleted (administrator rights required).
ui.whitelist.tooltip:
What to never delete. Examples:
*.log — all files with the .log extension
C:\Keep\file.txt — one specific file
re:\.bak$ — advanced rule (regular expression)

ui.privacy.protection.hint: Share of applied tweaks in the "Privacy" category. Turn them on in the "Optimization" page.
svc.note.system: A core Windows service. Do not stop it: the system may stop working.
svc.note.diagtrack: Sends diagnostics and telemetry data to Microsoft. Usually safe to disable.
svc.note.dmwappushservice: WAP push message service used by telemetry. Usually not needed.
svc.note.mapsbroker: Only needed for offline maps. Safe to disable if you do not use Windows Maps.
svc.note.retaildemo: Retail demo mode for stores. Not needed at home.
svc.note.fax: Sending and receiving faxes. Almost nobody needs it.
svc.note.xbox: Xbox services: sign-in and cloud saves. Safe to disable if you do not play Xbox games.
svc.note.wersvc: Sends error reports to Microsoft. Safe to disable.
svc.note.remoteregistry: Allows remote registry changes. Better to disable for security.
svc.note.lfsvc: Geolocation. Needed by apps that use your location.
svc.note.wmpnetworksvc: Network sharing of the media library. Usually not needed.
svc.note.trkwks: Tracks file links on the network. Usually not needed at home.
svc.note.wpcmonsvc: Parental controls. Safe to disable if you do not use them.
svc.note.sysmain: Speeds up app launches (Superfetch). Little effect on SSDs, but disabling can slow down HDDs.
svc.note.wsearch: Windows Search. Without it, search in Explorer and Start becomes slow.
svc.note.spooler: Print spooler. Printers will not work without it.
svc.note.wuauserv: Windows Update. Without it updates and security patches will not install.
svc.note.bthserv: Bluetooth support. Wireless devices will stop working without it.
svc.note.bits: Background file transfer, needed for updates and some programs.
svc.note.lanmanserver: File and printer sharing on the network. Other computers will not see your folders without it.
svc.note.termservice: Remote Desktop. You will not be able to connect to this computer remotely without it.
svc.note.audiosrv: Windows audio. Sound will stop working if you disable it.

safety.title: Before you begin
safety.intro: Cleaner is a beta. Start with analysis and review the results; choose only actions you understand.
safety.preview: 1. “Analyze without cleaning” shows what was found without deleting anything. Opening the app does not start cleanup or optimization.
safety.files: 2. Back up important files separately. Regular files go to quarantine, but some actions permanently delete data. Deleting quarantine is permanent.
safety.system: 3. Changes to Windows services and settings can affect your computer. Read the warnings; skip anything you are unsure about. Test unfamiliar system actions in a virtual machine.
safety.restore.title: We recommend creating a restore point
safety.restore.explain: It can help roll back Windows settings and system files, but cannot recover deleted personal files. Creating one needs administrator permission, takes time and uses disk space.
safety.restore.limits: System Protection must be enabled. Windows may refuse if a point was created within the last 24 hours. Cleaner does not change restore schedules, frequency or protection settings.
safety.reopen: Shown once for this Windows profile. You can reopen it in Settings. Continuing does not bypass confirmations for dangerous actions.
safety.creating: Preparing the restore point… Please wait for the result.
safety.created: A restore point is confirmed for this app session. You can continue.
safety.failed: A new point could not be confirmed. Check System Protection: Win + R → SystemPropertiesProtection.exe. Windows may require you to wait if a point was created recently. Skip system actions for now; you can explore the interface and analysis.
safety.restart.explain: Creating a point needs administrator permission. Windows will show a UAC prompt and Cleaner will restart. In the new window, click “Create a restore point” again. Cleanup and settings changes do not start automatically.
safety.restarting: Restarting Cleaner. Click create point again in the new window.
safety.restart.canceled: Restart was canceled or Windows did not allow it. No restore point was created. You can continue exploring the app.
safety.save.failed: Your acknowledgement could not be saved. Check access to the app settings file; this notice will appear again next time.
startup.handoff.failed: The previous Cleaner instance has not exited or the restart could not be verified. Close Cleaner and start the app again.
